Office Bearers
/ˈɒf.ɪs ˌbeə.rəz/
noun

The ones at the top of the organization chart and at the heart of every big decision.

President: The head of the society, steering the team and keeping the bigger picture in sight.

Treasurer: The numbers person, overseeing finances, logistics, and sponsorships to keep everything running smoothly.

General Secretary: The organisational backbone, handling administration, coordination, and event management.

Press Secretary: The voice and visual identity of the society, leading social media marketing, publications, graphics etc.

Directorate
/dɪˈrek.tər.ət/
noun
A collective of Directors and Deputy Directors, each leading a different portfolio and bringing their own skills, creativity, and a little bit of organised chaos to the society.

Spending money is inevitable, but what you can control is how and where you spend it. And
here budgeting is your best friend, so you don't run bone dry before your father gives you your
next pay.
1) Use the Metro Bus: With its stations going all the way to Saddar and multiple feeder
buses, it can save you a lot of money, and give you some fun stories to tell.
2) Try different street foods: Instead of spending huge amounts of money going to cafés, try
different street food. Your stomach might disagree sometimes, but your bank account
won't.
3) Thrift: Instead of spending a huge amount of money buying brand-new clothes, try the
H-9 Bazaar. You'll be surprised by the things you can find there. And if you have doubts,
remember: washing machines have been invented.
4) Choose low-cost activities: Go hiking, have a picnic, go window shopping with friends,
play board games, or come up with fun activities that aren't so hard on your wallet.
5) Get cheap friends: If your current friends are hard on your wallet, throw them out and get
cheapskates as friends. This will save you the money you spend trying to fit in.
6) Carry cash for daily spending: Take out only what you plan to spend that day. It's much
harder to accidentally spend Rs. 2,000 when you physically only have Rs. 500 in your
pocket.
7) Make a “fun money” limit: Don't completely ban yourself from spending. Give yourself a
fixed amount for cafés, snacks, shopping, etc.
8) Keep an emergency fund: Even if it's a small amount, keep some money aside for
unexpected expenses. Because somehow, the moment you're broke, everything
decides to go wrong at once.
9) Honestly, kbhi kbhi ghar aur hostel se bhi kha liya kro khana. Har roz bahar se khana
zaroori nahi hai. Ghar ka khana is literally right there. Hostel ka khana… Well, character development hai.
